headline: USA RARE EARTH SURGES 13% AS CRITICAL MINERALS REBOUND — Antimony +9%, MP Materials +6% in Sector-Wide Relief Rally
snippet: USA Rare Earth (USAR) jumped 13% on November 27 — reversing roughly half of its recent multi-day selloff — as a broad market risk-on session lifted the entire critical minerals complex. United States Antimony surged 9% and MP Materials gained 6%. The move follows two days of heavy selling tied to China extending its mineral export pause on gallium, germanium and antimony; analysts say Friday's rebound reflects short-covering and bargain hunting rather than any resolution of the underlying supply-chain tension.

headline: LYNAS POSTS RECORD 2,082 TONNE NdPr QUARTER AT AGM — Output Hits All-Time High as Rare Earth Stock Recovers 7%
snippet: Lynas Rare Earths (ASX: LYC) shares rebounded 7% on November 26 after the company reported record production of 2,082 tonnes of neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr) material at its AGM update — the highest single-quarter output in the company's history. The result gives Lynas a strengthening production case at a moment when most rare earth stocks have been punished by China-related trade uncertainty. Motley Fool's analysis argues the stock remains a buy on fundamentals despite recent sector-wide selling.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER RALLY LIFTS MINERS ACROSS THE BOARD — Junior and Mid-Cap Mining Stocks Recover After Month-Long Beatdown
snippet: Mining equities broadly advanced on November 27 as spot gold recovered above $3,600 and silver staged its strongest weekly close in a month. GoldSeek's coverage highlights that junior and mid-cap producers led the session, with the GDX and GDXJ both posting their best single-day gains in weeks. The rally arrives after gold fell roughly 26% from September highs and GDX entered a technical bear market, leaving technical indicators deeply oversold — conditions that historically attract systematic buying.

headline: AUSTRAL SNAPS UP HAMMER METALS' KALMAN COPPER DEPOSIT FOR $80.7M — Queensland Deal Closes; 1.29 Austral Shares Per Hammer Share
snippet: Austral Resources completed its $80.7 million acquisition of Hammer Metals on November 25, adding the Kalman copper deposit in Queensland to its portfolio through a scrip-based scheme of arrangement. Eligible Hammer Metals shareholders received 1.2903 new Austral shares per Hammer share held as of the November 18 record date. The deal follows the broader trend of well-capitalised copper producers acquiring exploration assets at multi-year valuation lows.

headline: GOLD MID-TIERS Q3'26: COSTS RISING FASTER THAN PRICES — Zeal Analysis Finds Margins Under Pressure Even at $3,500+ Gold
snippet: Adam Hamilton's quarterly deep-dive into gold mid-tier fundamentals for Q3 2026 finds that surging input costs — labour, fuel, consumables — are compressing profit margins that investors assumed would expand alongside gold prices. While mid-tier revenues hit near-record levels at $3,500+ gold, all-in sustaining costs at several companies rose faster than the gold price on a year-over-year basis. Hamilton argues the sector remains undervalued in absolute terms, but cautions that cost discipline is now the key differentiator between mid-tiers.

headline: SILVER MINERS CAN'T CLOSE THE SUPPLY GAP — Sixth Straight Annual Deficit Projected as Industrial Demand Swamps New Mine Output
snippet: A GoldSeek analysis published November 24 argues that primary silver miners are structurally unable to close the market's supply gap: despite a 3% increase in mine supply to 846.6 million ounces in 2025, the Silver Institute projects a sixth consecutive annual deficit of approximately 46–67 million ounces in 2026. Industrial demand — led by solar panels and EVs — continues to absorb new production, while 70-80% of silver is produced as a byproduct of base metal mines, limiting supply flexibility.

headline: SMM: COPPER BOTTOMED OUT NEAR $12,000 — Import Surge and Record Chinese Spot Premiums Signal LME Floor Is In
snippet: Shanghai Metals Market's weekly macro review released November 27 argues that LME copper has found a floor near $12,000–$12,300 per tonne, citing a surge in Chinese copper imports that is rebuilding inventory and pushing physical spot premiums toward recovery. SHFE copper futures were at 92,980 yuan/mt. SMM analysts note that while macro headwinds from Fed rate-hike expectations cap the upside, the structural demand signal from Chinese physical buying contradicts bearish futures-market positioning.

headline: WHICH GOLD MINERS HAVE A CUSHION? — At 15-Month Lows, Agnico Eagle and Kinross Named Best-Positioned While Barrick Faces Cuts
snippet: An Investing.com analysis published November 27 maps gold and silver miners by balance sheet strength as the GDX enters a technical bear market — all 12 of its tracked moving averages are now signaling sell. Bullion fell roughly 26% from September highs, but producers dropped 29–49%. Agnico Eagle and Kinross are cited as having the strongest financial buffers (net cash positions, low-cost operations), while Barrick and several mid-tiers face analyst estimate cuts as production fell year-over-year in Q3.

headline: GOLD DOESN'T PAY DIVIDENDS, BUT THESE 3 MINERS DO — Barrick 1.79%, Agnico Eagle, Newmont Yields Stand Out at Sector Lows
snippet: A November 27 analysis from 24/7 Wall St. argues that retail investors sitting on beaten-down gold producer positions can collect meaningful dividend yields while waiting for a recovery. Barrick Gold yields 1.79% at $34.53 — a price that reflects the brutal Q3-Q4 selloff — while Agnico Eagle and Newmont offer their own payouts backed by some of the industry's strongest balance sheets. The piece frames dividends as a way to hold conviction in a sector trading near multi-year valuation floors.

headline: WALL STREET SEES 60-78% UPSIDE IN KINROSS, OCEANA GOLD, ALAMOS — Strong Buy Consensus Builds as Stocks Trade Well Below Analyst Targets
snippet: TipRanks identifies Kinross Gold, OceanaGold, and Alamos Gold as three gold producers with Street-consensus Strong Buy ratings and analyst price targets implying 63–78% upside from current levels. All three are mid-tier producers with North American or Australian-Pacific operations, lower geopolitical risk profiles than global majors, and production costs that remain economic at current gold prices well above $3,000. The piece acknowledges the disconnect: analyst targets assume gold stabilises and re-rates, while spot gold is still under Fed-hike pressure.

headline: F4 URANIUM RAISES C$1.5M IN PRIVATE PLACEMENT — TSX-V Junior Funds Saskatchewan Uranium Exploration at 90-Cent Metal Prices
snippet: F4 Uranium (TSX-V: FFU) announced a non-brokered private placement of up to C$1.5 million on November 27, earmarked to advance its Saskatchewan uranium exploration portfolio. The raise is a signal that junior uranium companies can still access capital even with URNM down 31% year-to-date, buoyed by uranium spot prices holding near $90/lb — a level that makes Saskatchewan exploration economics compelling for patient investors. F4's project pipeline is in the Athabasca Basin, North America's highest-grade uranium district.
